channel.title: AI Frontier Post
channel.description: Dispatches from the AI frontier: AI news, research explainers, frontier lab coverage, and product comparisons.

item.title: Stop trusting the contract: ship an AI feature on Vercel AI Gateway with Audited ZDR
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Vercel now audits zero-data-retention claims instead of taking providers' word for it — and runs canary traps that catch any provider reading your prompts. This tutorial wires Audited ZDR into a real AI SDK app: per-request flags, the team-wide toggle, headquarters filtering, and a canary check you can run yourself.

item.title: Microsoft answers OpenAI's shared-limits call: MAI-2 Base scores 0.819 on OpenAI's own test
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Mustafa Suleyman backed Jakub Pachocki's proposal for shared perplexity limits — and disclosed that Microsoft's in-house MAI-2 Base scores 0.819 log-perplexity on OpenAI's evaluation set, in the same ballpark as GPT-5.6 Sol.

item.title: OpenAI opens 50,000 free ChatGPT grants to academic researchers — first come, first served
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Applications open today for the next round of ChatGPT for Academic Researchers: 50,000 grants, each covering a researcher and up to two collaborators with a year of ChatGPT Plus, as OpenAI doubles the program's target to 200,000 scientists worldwide.

item.title: Evaluate your RAG pipeline with DeepEval: a complete local eval suite with a free Ollama judge
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Stop vibe-checking your RAG app. DeepEval 4.3.4 turns output quality into pytest tests — faithfulness, answer relevancy, contextual precision, and custom G-Eval criteria — scored by a local Ollama model, with no API key and no data leaving your machine.

item.title: White House says Trump was 'totally involved' in bringing Jensen Huang back — and Trump says Nvidia would be 'very sad' without him
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Hours after Nvidia's board voted to bring Jensen Huang back, the White House moved to claim the credit: a spokesperson says President Trump was 'totally involved' in the return — a claim that goes well beyond what the board itself said about the government's role.

item.title: Governors draw a federalism line on AI: Washington handles the big risks, states keep the rest
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: The National Governors Association released six bipartisan principles for AI governance, telling the incoming Congress that Washington should handle national risks while states keep authority over how AI is used.

item.title: Turn your coding agent into a marketer: hands-on with marketingskills' 53 skills
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: marketingskills packs 53 marketing skills — copywriting, SEO, CRO, analytics — into one MIT collection that installs into Claude Code, Codex and Cursor with a single command. This tutorial installs three of them and runs a full marketing workflow on a fictional SaaS, end to end, with no API key.

item.title: California widens its Nvidia probe to possible criminal violations over China chip sales
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Attorney General Rob Bonta says the investigation into whether Nvidia’s chips or secrets reached China — and whether investors were misled — now spans criminal as well as civil law. The probe is preliminary, and no wrongdoing has been found.

item.title: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO — unanimous board vote, with U.S. government input
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Eleven days after Jensen Huang resigned, Nvidia’s board has voted unanimously to bring him back as president and CEO, effective immediately — after taking input from senior levels of the U.S. government on the national-security questions around him.

item.title: China Telecom open-sources Xing4.1-Preview: a 285B agentic model trained entirely on Huawei Ascend chips
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: China Telecom has released the open weights of Xing4.1-Preview, a 285-billion-parameter agentic model trained end to end on Huawei Ascend chips — no Nvidia hardware anywhere in the stack. Its benchmarks are mid-pack, but the hardware story is the point.

item.title: After a decade of talks, 128 states agree to draft rules for lethal autonomous weapons — but not whether they will bind
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: States meeting in Geneva agreed to spend 2027 and 2028 drafting an international instrument on lethal autonomous weapons — the first mandate of its kind after more than a decade of talks. Whether the rules will be legally binding was left for the end of negotiations.

item.title: One plugin collection for every coding agent: hands-on with wshobson/agents
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: wshobson/agents packs 93 plugins, 199 agents, 185 skills and 103 commands into one Markdown source that installs into Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode and more. The skills-only path is fully run-verified — no account, no API key.

item.title: GLM-5.4 hands-on: run Z.ai's new vision coding model inside Claude Code
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Z.ai's GLM-5.4 landed on November 23 with vision input, a million-token context, and 50% more weekly quota. Here's the full setup — Claude Code, the Vision MCP server, effort controls, and the credit math — verified against Z.ai's own docs.

item.title: Bezos says his Prometheus AI redesigned the Mars helicopter from a prompt — and the clip has Reddit asking for proof
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: A 100-second clip of Jeff Bezos saying his AI startup Prometheus redesigned NASA's Mars helicopter from a prompt hit r/accelerate on Sunday night — and the thread's top replies want proof, not promises.

item.title: Together AI discloses prompt leak after an AI coding agent exposed a repo credential
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: An AI coding agent committed a credential to a public repository, and an unauthorized party downloaded stored customer prompts from Together AI’s serverless inference service. Five of the credentials the intruder tested belonged to a Dragos canary experiment.

item.title: Z.ai ships GLM-5.4: vision, a million-token context, and 50% more quota for coding subscribers
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Z.ai’s new flagship coding model adds vision and a million-token context window, with 50% more weekly quota for Coding Plan subscribers — but no benchmarks, pricing, or open-weight plans yet.

item.title: Meta's Alexandr Wang: superintelligence is arriving — and the next year matters most
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Meta's chief AI officer says superintelligence is arriving, pointing to the claimed Riemann proof as the opening moment — and argues that how humanity acts over the next year will have great consequence.

item.title: A 4 MB voice that runs anywhere: hands-on with Kitten-TTS-2 Pico, Nano and Mini
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: KittenML's new tiny voices — Pico at 4 MB, Nano at 8.8 MB, Mini at 47.5 MB — run faster than real time on a single CPU thread. Here's how to install them, pick a voice, switch languages, and choose the right size.

item.title: Musk: Tesla's cars run a real-time world model — and the 25-second video has Reddit arguing over what it actually is
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: A 25-second clip of a Tesla touchscreen rendering a photorealistic downtown street went viral after Elon Musk said the cars carry a smaller version of the “pixel-perfect” world model Tesla has used for synthetic data since last year. The comments immediately started arguing about whether it is diffusion, mean-flow, or Gaussian splatting — and what “~1B” even means.

item.title: Cognition launches Devin Bots: AI managers that run teams of coding agents for weeks
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Cognition’s Devin Bots hand a whole engineering goal — not a task — to a persistent AI manager that plans, delegates, and keeps the context for weeks. The showcase is an Android app built in 44 days; the catch is that every number comes from Cognition itself.

item.title: Replit launches Missions: give an agent swarm a goal and a budget, and it plans, builds, and tests
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Replit’s new Missions product hands a whole project — not a prompt — to a swarm of AI agents working inside a budget and approval rules you set. Its headline proof, an internal monitoring platform built in two days for $3,000, comes with caveats worth reading first.

item.title: Catch prompt theft before your users do: build a canary-token tripwire for your LLM app
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: OpenRouter just cut three providers after researchers caught them stealing prompts with canary tokens. Here is how to run the same test on your own app — with a free local model, in an afternoon.

item.title: A Reddit user built a working GTA-style game in a day with Gemini Neon — and the comments did the fact-checking
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: A 2:15 gameplay video posted to r/GeminiAI shows a low-poly open-world game — driving, carjacking, NPC chaos — built in about a day by someone who says they have no idea what they are doing. It hit 1,900 upvotes in seven hours, and the top comments immediately started pulling the claim apart.

item.title: Tesla Cybercab stops as human driver keeps going in viral Austin crash video
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: A 12-second clip from downtown Austin shows Tesla's driverless Cybercab stopping while a human-driven car keeps going — and crashes. Posted on Friday night, it passed 1.4 million views on X and set off a familiar argument about who the safer driver really is.

item.title: Hundreds of AI agents are tackling P vs NP live, with Lean checking every lemma
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: A self-funded fleet of AI agents is attacking the most famous open problem in computer science — live, in public, with every lemma checked by Lean. Nothing is solved yet. That is the point.
